items.recapEn: In hot Mishima, where Fuji's spring water runs through the town, Hana and Ken read the shrine board: photos allowed here, none inside, no eating. Nakamura-san said feet in the water were fine, so they cooled theirs. Over cold soba Ken explained why he cooks: his mother worked late, and he fed his sister. Tomorrow the water reaches Numazu's fish.

items.recapEn: By the stream Hana asked whether she could put her feet in; Ken said yes, but no running. She asked why he became a cook: his mother worked late, so he cooked eggs and vegetables for his sister every night, and a meal alone tasted bad. Tomorrow he will buy fish in Numazu.

items.recapEn: The rules board at Mishima Taisha, as Hana copied it: walk quietly, wash your hands at the entrance, photos outside but not inside the buildings, no eating in the grounds though water and tea are fine, bicycles and phone calls stay at the gate, hats may stay on in the heat, and ask Nakamura if anything is unclear.
